quote: Consider for illustration of the theorem 4.1, the sample X1, X2, X3, X4, X5 from U(0,1) with n = 4 and n + 1 = 5. Now we know that X_{k:n} ~ Beta(k, n + 1 - k). Now we take l from Gumbel-Hougaard Copula ... as the appropriate stdf for Archimax copula model with 5-monotone Archimedean generator phi(t) = e^{-t^{1/theta}}, theta in [1, infty), where stable tail dependence function (stdf) is l(x) = (x_1^theta + x_2^theta + ... + x_n^theta)^{1/theta} with l(x) = ||x||A(x/||x||). For reverse hazard rate ordering, we calculate t phi'(t)/phi(t) = -(1/theta) t^{1/theta} which is a decreasing function of t >= 0, because for theta in [1, infty), we get d/dt (-(1/theta) t^{1/theta}) = -(1/theta^2) t^{1/theta - 1} <= 0 for all t >= 0. On the other hand F_{X_{5:5}} = x, F_{X_{4:4}} = 4x^3 - 3x^4 and equating both expression of l we have A = n^{1/theta - 1} with n = 4. Plots are shown below which illustrates the theorem 4.1 (i) for theta = 4.
